topics.name: Section A Reading information and ideas: two unseen non-fiction texts (19th century and 20th or 21st century)
points: Identifying and interpreting key ideas and information from texts
Question 1: short retrieval and explanation questions on the first text (AO1)
Question 2: summarising and synthesising similarities across both texts (6 marks)
Question 3: analysing how a writer uses language and structure, with subject terminology (AO2, 12 marks)
Question 4: evaluating a statement about both texts and comparing how they present it (AO4 and AO3, 18 marks)
Effects of writing for particular audiences and purposes; context such as historical setting, mode or genre
Evaluating usefulness: identifying bias and misuse of evidence
Exploring connections across texts in terms of ideas, attitudes and values

topics.name: Section B Writing for audience, impact and purpose
points: Question 5 or 6: one extended non-fiction writing task linked to the reading theme (40 marks)
Writing to describe, explain, inform, instruct, argue and persuade in forms such as articles, speeches and letters
Selecting and emphasising key ideas; citing evidence and quotation; writing to create emotional impact
Adapting tone, style and register; maintaining a consistent viewpoint
Organising ideas clearly and coherently for audience and purpose (AO5, 24 marks)
Range of sentence structures, vocabulary, accurate spelling and punctuation (AO6, 16 marks)

topics.name: Section A Reading meaning and effects: two 20th- or 21st-century prose fiction or literary non-fiction texts
points: Question 1: short retrieval and explanation questions on the first text (AO1)
Question 2: analysing language and structure in a short section (AO2, 6 marks)
Question 3: exploring how the writer uses language and structure, with subject terminology (AO2, 12 marks)
Question 4: evaluating a statement about both texts and comparing them (AO4 and AO3, 18 marks)
Interpreting writers' meanings and effects within and across texts; identifying main themes and ideas
Evaluating how form and structure contribute to effectiveness and impact
Exploring connections across texts in terms of ideas, attitudes and values

topics.name: Section B Writing imaginatively and creatively
points: Question 5 or 6: one extended creative writing task, e.g. a story or a description, linked to the reading theme (40 marks)
Organising and structuring narrative writing to create deliberate effects
Narrative point of view and maintaining a consistent viewpoint
Choices of vocabulary and grammar to create deliberate effects; using language creatively
Using wide reading of prose fiction and literary non-fiction to inform technique (AO5, 24 marks)
Range of sentence structures, accurate spelling and punctuation (AO6, 16 marks)

topics.name: Spoken Language endorsement (non-exam assessment)
points: Selecting and organising information and ideas for a prepared formal presentation, agreed in advance with the teacher
Planning for different purposes and audiences; presentation formats (talk, speech, debate or dialogue)
Giving the presentation in a formal setting (up to about ten minutes)
Listening and responding appropriately to questions and feedback
Using spoken Standard English
Pass, Merit and Distinction criteria; graded separately and not part of the 9 to 1 grade
